[2.4.4](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x11-V2-Authentication.md#v24-credential-storage)

> Verify that if bcrypt is used, the work factor SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, with a minimum of 10.

Issue is "spin off" from discussion in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/756#issuecomment-642144272

Proposal from @tghosth is not implemented and the question is - is it so by accident?

> V2.4.4 Verify that if bcrypt is used, the work factor SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow (typically at least 13) **and passwords are pre-hashed to avoid truncation issues**.

comments.body: Pre-hashing has significant limits and leads to broken implementations so I am suggesting limiting passwords to 72 bytes instead on purpose.

> Pre-hashing has significant limits and leads to broken implementations so I am suggesting limiting passwords to 72 bytes instead on purpose.

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/756#issuecomment-638781209 - here is your opinion opposite of that, what is the reason/argumentation for that change?

I’ve been made aware if the many things that can go wrong with prehashing and it adds a later of sometimes fragile complexity. Using a algorithm that dosn't require this awkward step, like Argon2id or even scrypt is preferred.

Can you make others also aware?

With this requirement text context using other algorithm is not an option.

One, there is the problem is password shucking
https://www.scottbrady91.com/authentication/beware-of-password-shucking#:~:text=Password%20shucking%20is%20a%20method,it%20to%20its%20weaker%20algorithm.

Two, prehashing is not as simple as it looks.  From https://security.stackexchange.com/questions/61595/is-it-good-practice-to-sha512-passwords-prior-to-passing-them-to-bcrypt

_You still want to exercise caution about some practical details. In particular, many bcrypt implementations expect a password, i.e. a sequence of characters, terminating with the first byte of value 0x00. The output of SHA-512 is binary and thus may contain some bytes of value 0x00. For instance, 1/256th of all passwords will yield a hash value which begins with a byte of value 0x00, that a string-based bcrypt instance will understand as equivalent to an empty password._

Three, the canonical implementations of bcrypt silently truncate after 72 bytes https://passlib.readthedocs.io/en/stable/lib/passlib.hash.bcrypt.html

The password section is heavily modified and in parity with https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html - please open a new issue if you want to make major changes. I am happy to adjust 2.4.4 and add the 72-byte limit.
